page: Microsoft Azure E16as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V architecture. It features a dedicated 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor delivering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio. Cache hierarchy details include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. The underlying hardware platform does not include bundled local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, requiring external premium managed disks for persistent storage operations.

Hardware vector extensions include AVX-512 support with VNNI and BF16 capabilities, complemented by standard hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. Synthetic benchmarks reflect strong single-core CPU throughput and text processing efficiency, with Geekbench and stress-ng tests placing single-threaded performance in the upper quartile. Multi-core performance metrics align with mid-range baselines, recording 22.08 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 20.88 GB per second in static web serving benchmarks. Memory evaluation demonstrates stable cached read bandwidth, though large uncached block reads register lower relative throughput.

The absence of integrated local storage necessitates careful planning around remote block storage performance and network I/O latencies. By allocating a high ratio of RAM per dedicated core, the instance provides cost-efficient memory density for infrastructure tiers that do not demand expansive compute counts. Microsoft Azure E16as_v6 is primarily suited for in-memory databases, distributed key-value caches like Redis, data transformation pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise business applications.
description: Microsoft Azure E16as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 128 GB of memory, it provides an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-heavy computing. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not bundle local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying on external network-attached storage for persistence. Benchmark results highlight strong single-core compute and text processing performance alongside consistent mid-tier multi-core execution and memory throughput. However, large uncached read memory bandwidth is comparatively limited, and larger language model inference shows diminished efficiency. With its high RAM density relative to compute allocation, the E16as_v6 serves in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, enterprise application runtimes, and large memory data processing tasks requiring dedicated processing threads.
